newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil primary public sector surplus seen in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil primary public sector surplus seen in 1997.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Ministry Executive Secretary Pedro Parente said the government expected to achieve a primary public sector surplus, which excludes interest paid on debt, of 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997.
Parente, who was speaking at a lunch with businessmen in Rio de Janeiro, declined to make any forecast on next year's operational public sector deficit.

"Because the operational deficit includes a component which depends on interest rates which are influenced by other economic factors, the government cannot set an operational target but only a primary target with regard to the fiscal situation," he said.

Last month, Finance Minister Pedro Malan announced a fiscal package designed to bring down the operational public sector deficit to 2.5 percent of GDP in 1997 from between 3.5 and four percent this year.
